answer_text: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field: the forefinger points along the field, the middle finger along the current, and the thumb then gives the motion. In an electric motor a rectangular coil sits between the poles of a magnet. Current in the two long sides is opposite, so the forces on those sides form a couple and the coil turns. A split-ring commutator reverses the current every half rotation so the couple always acts in the same sense and the coil keeps spinning.
